result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.reverse()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Reverse the direction of all edges in the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14776-L14854){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.reverse() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Reverse edges](/assets/graphs/reverse.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A directed graph on A, B, C, D with arrows A to B, B to C, D to C, and A to D. After reverse(), the same four edges point the opposite way, B to A, C to B, C to D, and D to A, all drawn in the accent color." width="100%"} Creates a new graph with the same nodes but all edge directions reversed (`u->v` becomes `v->u`). For undirected graphs, returns a new copy (no structural change). Preserves all node and edge attributes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph with reversed edge directions. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#321d91c4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec original = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "C") ) reversed_graph = original.reverse() original.has_edge("A", "B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: ::: The original graph is untouched -- `reverse()` returns a new graph where every edge now points the other way: ::: {#b1f1d782 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} reversed_graph.has_edge("B", "A") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: This is handy for working out what depends on what: reversing a "provides" relationship turns it into a "depends on" one: ::: {#0b51ad51 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} deps = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B", label="provides") .add_edge("B", "C", label="provides") ) dependents = deps.reverse() dependents.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['B->A', 'C->B'] ``` ::: ::: Some algorithms, like finding strongly connected components, need both a graph and its transpose: ::: {#b90bb042 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.Graph(directed=True) g.add_node(label="X") g.add_node(label="Y") g.add_node(label="Z") g.add_edge("X", "Y") g.add_edge("Y", "Z") g_transpose = g.reverse() g_transpose.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['Y->X', 'Z->Y'] ``` ::: :::
